usage: A common everyday noun for a cutting tool; in gardening contexts it often means pruning shears or garden scissors.
Usually used as a standalone countable noun; if you need one pair, Cantonese often says 一把剪刀.
Can refer to general scissors, not only garden tools, so context decides whether it means kitchen, school, or gardening shears.
For polite or practical requests, it is often paired with verbs like 借, 搵, 拎, or 用.
